observations: 1) REAL failure clip: From 00:00.000 to 00:04.125, the robot sits stationary on a wooden floor facing a gap between a staircase on the left and kitchen island barstools on the right. At 00:04.250, it drives straight forward without steering away from the barstool legs. At 00:08.500–00:09.375, its right side collides with the front barstool leg, flipping the robot onto its side (confirmed by the IMU log around t=7.06s–7.86s where ay_g shifts to ~1.02g and az_g drops to ~0g), where it remains through 00:11.875.

2) OLD policy in the twin: From 00:00.000 to 00:01.250, the robot drives straight forward toward the obstacle on its right. Between 00:01.375 and 00:01.750, the front-right corner of the robot strikes the obstacle head-on (min_clearance 0.035 m) and the episode terminates in a collision at 00:01.800.

3) NEW policy in the twin: From 00:00.000 to 00:01.500, the robot smoothly steers left to give the obstacle a wide berth. Between 00:01.500 and 00:02.750, it passes the obstacle safely with 0.307 m clearance (and at least 0.249 m across all 40 randomized variants). From 00:02.750 to 00:04.600, it smoothly counter-steers to realign with its original forward heading and completes the maneuver without oscillation, stalling, or collision.
